 News › News News › CBSE Board Exams 2027: Here's what parents need to know ahead of the release of CBSE date sheet CBSE Board Exams 2027: Here's what parents need to know ahead of the release of CBSE date sheet
 Jasleen Taneja Updated: Nov 6, 2026, 16:16 IST Parents should replace “How much have you studied?” with “How are you feeling today?” CBSE Board Date Sheet 2027 class 10, 12 is expected to be released anytime soon in PDF form on the official website. During this time, parents can help their children prepare for the exam by checking the official syllabus, reviewing sample question papers, planning regular revision and staying in touch with the school officials.
 The aim is to create a realistic study routine, identifying gaps and supporting their children by providing them a calm environment, encouragement and practical support.
 CBSE Board Exams 2027 : Important guidelines for parents 
 CBSE publishes examination notices, syllabus and important updates on its website. Parents should keep a track of the official website regularly to get the important updates. Parents must keep in mind the following things.
 Keep a track of CBSE datesheet: Look for official examination schedule. Do not rely on social media posts or forwarded messages
 Check the syllabus: Parents must check the syllabus released by CBSE. They should keep an eye whether the child is preparing as per the syllabus or not.
 Follow school notices: Parents must keep an eye on practical exam notices. Besides, they should also know about the internal assessments, attendance and other school requirements.
 Verify registration details: Ask school to confirm student’s personal details and selected subjects are correct or not
 Identify the gaps: Instead of asking the child to study every subject for same number of hours, identify the specific learning gaps.
 During board exams, the most useful thing parents can offer is not another study timetable but a calm home. Keep mealtimes, sleep and routines predictable, and let your child take real breaks without guilt. Replace “How much have you studied?” with “How are you feeling today?” Praise effort and consistency, not just marks, and avoid comparing them with cousins or classmates. Sometimes, simply sitting nearby with a cup of tea says “I’m here” better than words.
